turns.t: Mr Hartley, I'm Chloe, the nurse. You came in with a wrist injury. Let me get your pulse and blood pressure. ~
Thank you, my dear. I'm afraid I've been rather foolish. I fell off a ladder, cleaning the gutters.
Pulse 88, blood pressure 144 over 86, temperature 36.7.
Good morning, Mr Hartley. I'm Dr Naylor. Tell me what happened. ~
I was about eight feet up, and the ladder slipped, and I came down on my left hand, with my arm out.
When was that?
About two hours ago. And my wrist has swollen up, rather alarmingly.
How bad is the pain?
Severe when I move it. I can hardly turn my hand over.
Did you hit your head, or hurt anywhere else?
No, no head injury. My right knee is a bit sore, but nothing much.
Any numbness or tingling in your fingers?
A little tingling in my thumb and index finger.
Do you have any medical problems?
High blood pressure and an underactive thyroid.
And do you do anything which might affect healing, do you smoke?
I gave up thirty years ago.
Let me look at your wrist. Tell me when it hurts.
Ow! There. ~
The wrist is swollen, with a visible bump, a deformity, on the back of it, it's very tender over the end of the radius, and the fingers are warm with a good pulse.
His capillary refill is normal, doctor. ~
Thank you, Chloe. Mr Hartley, this looks like a broken wrist, a fracture of the radius, called a Colles' fracture.
Oh, bother. ~
I can't be certain without an X-ray, and it could also involve a small bone in the wrist, so I'd like an X-ray of the wrist, and one of the knee.
Can I have something for the pain? ~
Chloe will give you something strong right away. ~
I'll bring it now. ~
Please keep the arm raised on a pillow, and don't eat or drink anything until the X-rays are done, in case you need it set.
Will it need to be put back? ~
Possibly. If the bone has shifted, we'll set it under local anaesthetic, in the department. ~
How very modern. ~
Chloe will take you through to radiology. If your fingers go cold, blue or numb, tell her at once.
I shall. Thank you. ~
